Are you creating your own patterns? Is so, what is your process?

I do create my own patterns. But with this pouch I just did a Google search for it.

If I'm making my own pattern (like with this gorget and pauldron set) I start with designing everything in Photoshop based on general body measurements. I have an 11x17 printer for the larger pieces. After printing and cutting out, I transfer the pattern onto some underlayment. This is a great material as it's very cheap for a lot, has enough rigidity to hold shape, but still very malleable.

At this point the underlayment will become my main pattern. I mark out the holes and punch them, then using brads I can put the entire project together to make sure everything fits (example of an articulated elbow). This has saved me from wasting a ton of leather.

From there it's straight forward. Mark out the shapes on the leather using my pattern and cut. I'm currently working on a second pouch that's 5.5"x6" with a 3" gusset. The double loop lacing I'm doing to tie it together has been a long process but it looks great. Once it's finished I'll post it up here.
What did you use to dye it that green color?

For the gusset I used Fiebing's Oil Dye in green. This was the first time I've used Oil dye and I can't say that I'm a fan. For me it's very hard to control the spread, which can leave some nasty splotches throughout the piece. It also goes VERY quickly. I did a few test pieces with my brown dyes and had already gone through half the bottle. No good.

For my money I prefer Tandy's EcoFlow. Apply liberally and wipe off the excess.
Good to know. I've been using the Fiebing's Oil dyes recently and I have to admit that it's hard to get an even finish. My pieces end up looking blotchy.

Yeah, pick up some EcoFlo when you get a chance. I also really enjoy the Gel version as well. You just work it into the leather with a soft cloth (I actually use mechanics towels, those blue ones) and eventually the leather will just soak it all up for a great finish.

In fact I did this armor using the gel.

Something that helped me when I was trying to learn some programming was to set a schedule, an hour a day at a specific time slot where I'd make myself sit down and learn. Everyone is different, but that worked well for me, and it's something that carrys over to anything you are trying to do. If you have goals you want to work towards, but see yourself making little to no progress, make a schedule and follow it. I know it sounds like simple advice, but working towards your goal whenever you feel like it tends to not work well. Set aside some time each day, make sure to set aside a specific time slot. Otherwise you'll say "oh I can do it later", "maybe later", "it's too late now, I'm tired. Maybe tomorrow". Set aside a specific time slot and make yourself stop anything else you are doing. But be careful, know your limits. 3 hours a day 5 days a week, then 8 hours a day weekends might sound fine to you now, when you're pumped and ready to go. But you'll burn yourself out and end up skipping a day. Then comes a downward spiral of skipping.

Try to pace yourself and keep up your morale. Don't just look at the big goal at the end, your morale will drain pretty quick when you realize how slowly you're getting to your goal. Instead, keep your end goal in mind but make smaller goals all along the way. Maybe decide what you want to get done for the week, and work towards that.

If you find that your morale dropped and you're back to making no progress, then don't just passively accept that and wait for your motivation to come back. Weeks or even months can go by until your mood changes. Sit down and have a word with yourself. "Alright, I didn't follow my schedule yesterday/the past few days, I was too tired and I just didn't feel like it. Now this week's goal just seems out of reach. I can't let that happen again, I need to break out of my downward spiral. I'll readjust my goal for this week according to how much time I have left, and I'll work towards that goal starting right now. Even if my scheduled time slot already passed, and I could just wait until tomorrow's scheduled time slot, I need to break out of my spiral immediately."

Try to assess what made you give up. Maybe your mood just went south and you weren't up for it. Adjust to correct. Make sure you are getting enough sleep, not pulling all nighters on Voat. Unplug or take the batteries out of whatever can distract you and force yourself to work towards your goal even if you are not up for it. Maybe the problem really is that you're just overworking yourself. Don't judge that just on your mood, actually take a look at your schedule. Are you leaving yourself with only an hour or two of free time and relaxing, but 3 or more hours of working towards your goal? It sounds like time management could be the problem, you may need more time to unwind. Maybe you can adjust that to just 2 or 1 hours of working towards your goal. Do you have 5 hours of free time plus 1 or 2 hours of working towards your goal? Well then time management probably isn't the problem. Breaking out of a downward spiral isn't easy, you will need to push yourself to do something you do not feel like doing.
